maximum_permitted_stay: Up to 6 months per visit under Standard Visitor permission, subject to the permission granted.
entry_count: Single or multiple entry as issued
passport_validity_rule: Passport must be valid for the whole intended stay; no additional six-month post-expiry validity rule is stated in UKVI guidance.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No universal minimum was stated in the accessible IOM/UKVI/VFS Bangladesh guidance reviewed; follow the personalised checklist and confirm with VFS if a blank page is requested.
return_ticket_rule: Must satisfy the decision-maker that you will leave at the end of the visit and can pay for return or onward travel; a prepaid ticket is not universally required.
proof_of_funds_rule: Show sufficient accessible funds for reasonable trip costs and return or onward travel; no fixed minimum balance is published. Sponsor support must be evidenced.
accommodation_rule: Provide the address and arrangements for where you will stay; a prepaid hotel booking is not a universal requirement and is weak evidence by itself.
travel_insurance_rule: No mandatory visitor travel-insurance requirement was identified in the reviewed IOM/UKVI visitor rules; insurance is recommended but is not a visa condition.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: No general health or vaccination certificate requirement was identified for an ordinary visit of up to six months; itinerary-specific health rules may apply.
transit_rule: UK airport transit is governed by UK transit rules. A valid UKVI visitor visa permits Isle of Man visits without a separate IOM visa. Do not assume an Irish-route exemption applies to a Bangladesh passport; confirm route-specific permission before travel.
application_channel: GOV.UK/UKVI online application; VFS UK VAC in Dhaka or Sylhet for biometrics and documents. A valid UKVI visitor visa permits Isle of Man visits without a separate IOM visa.
processing_time: IOM visit applications from outside Isle of Man/UK: up to 13 weeks (estimate, not guarantee).

review_notes: Bangladesh ordinary passport, tourism/visitor. Current Isle of Man public guidance confirms that a valid visa issued by the UK Home Office/UKVI, Jersey or Guernsey permits a visit to the Isle of Man without a separate IOM visa. The current UK Home Office Appendix Visitor list includes Bangladesh, so the established route for a Bangladeshi ordinary-passport tourist is a UK Standard Visitor visa that is valid for the Isle of Man. The Home Office fee table explicitly labels the Standard Visitor visa as covering the UK, Isle of Man, Jersey and Guernsey. Bangladesh fees checked 15 November 2026: BDT 22,997 (up to 6 months), BDT 86,197 (2 years), BDT 153,825 (5 years), BDT 192,154 (10 years); the 6-month UK fee is GBP 135. VFS optional services are separate. The Isle of Man Immigration Service currently estimates up to 13 weeks for visit applications made from outside the Isle of Man/UK; this is an estimate, not a guarantee, and must not be replaced with the generic UKVI three-week estimate. GOV.UK says Standard Visitor applicants apply online, attend a VAC appointment, provide fingerprints and a photo, and successful UKVI applications receive an eVisa. This is distinct from Isle of Man-specific entry clearance, whose digital status from 1 July 2026 is expressly not an eVisa; evisa_available remains false to avoid describing the Isle of Man as issuing its own eVisa. A valid UKVI eVisa can still be used as the qualifying visa for IOM entry. Photo research: the standard Bangladesh biometric route captures a facial photograph at the VFS UK VAC; no universal printed or digital dimensions are published for this route. If biometric enrolment is waived, follow the personalised UKVI/VFS instruction; VAC capture does not prove a separate photo is never required. UKVI supporting-document guidance is circumstance-specific: there is no universal fixed bank balance, prepaid hotel booking or purchased return ticket requirement. The current Isle of Man Immigration Rules page links a version effective 2 November 2026, but its PDF returned HTTP 403 in this research session. The core UKVI-visa route is nevertheless supported by current Isle of Man public guidance, the current UK visa-national list and the Bangladesh-specific Home Office fee table. If a traveller does not hold a valid UKVI/Jersey/Guernsey visa and seeks Isle of Man-specific entry clearance, they should obtain direct confirmation from the Isle of Man Immigration Service about the current Appendix 2 route before travel. The VFS Bangladesh portal confirms the Dhaka and Sylhet centres, but its dynamic personalised 'what to bring' checklist was not independently retrievable; no minimum blank-page count or exempt-biometric photo specification is asserted. Follow the current personalised checklist.
